papers.title: ESPEI for efficient thermodynamic database development, modification, and uncertainty quantification: application to Cu-Mg
papers.abstract: The software package ESPEI has been developed for efficient evaluation of thermodynamic model parameters within the CALPHAD method. ESPEI uses a linear fitting strategy to parameterize Gibbs energy functions of single phases based on their thermochemical data and refine the model parameters using phase equilibrium data through Bayesian optimization within a Markov Chain Monte Carlo machine learning approach. In this paper, the methodologies employed in ESPEI are discussed in detail and demonstrated for the Cu-Mg system down to 0 K using unary descriptions based on segmented regression. The model parameter uncertainties are quantified and propagated to the Gibbs energy functions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法用于热力学数据库开发，与生物力学或植入物设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on thermodynamic CALPHAD modeling, not on FEA surrogate modeling, implant biomechanics, or any biomedical application.

summary_zh.motivation: 高效开发热力学数据库并量化参数不确定性。
summary_zh.method: 使用贝叶斯优化和MCMC机器学习方法拟合吉布斯自由能参数。
summary_zh.result: 成功应用于Cu-Mg系统，量化了模型参数不确定性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过Cu-Mg系统的热化学和相平衡数据验证。

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently develop thermodynamic databases with quantified parameter uncertainties using the CALPHAD method.
summary_en.method: A linear fitting strategy combined with Bayesian optimization and Markov Chain Monte Carlo is employed to parameterize Gibbs energy functions.
summary_en.result: The approach is demonstrated on the Cu-Mg system, yielding quantified uncertainties in model parameters propagated to Gibbs energies.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed using thermochemical and phase equilibrium data for the Cu-Mg system.

papers.title: Predictive Uncertainty Quantification with Compound Density Networks
papers.abstract: Despite the huge success of deep neural networks (NNs), finding good mechanisms for quantifying their prediction uncertainty is still an open problem. Bayesian neural networks are one of the most popular approaches to uncertainty quantification. On the other hand, it was recently shown that ensembles of NNs, which belong to the class of mixture models, can be used to quantify prediction uncertainty. In this paper, we build upon these two approaches. First, we increase the mixture model's flexibility by replacing the fixed mixing weights by an adaptive, input-dependent distribution (specifying the probability of each component) represented by NNs, and by considering uncountably many mixture components. The resulting class of models can be seen as the continuous counterpart to mixture density networks and is therefore referred to as compound density networks (CDNs). We employ both maximum likelihood and variational Bayesian inference to train CDNs, and empirically show that they yield better uncertainty estimates on out-of-distribution data and are more robust to adversarial examples than the previous approaches.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种新的不确定性量化方法，可迁移至代理模型，提高预测可靠性。
llm.why_not_core: No application to FEA surrogate modeling or biomechanical design; no constraint handling or multi-objective optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 深度神经网络缺乏可靠的不确定性量化机制。
summary_zh.method: 提出复合密度网络，结合自适应混合权重与连续混合成分。
summary_zh.result: 在分布外数据和对抗样本上不确定性估计更优。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准基准数据集上对比最大似然与变分贝叶斯训练。

summary_en.motivation: Deep neural networks lack reliable mechanisms for quantifying prediction uncertainty.
summary_en.method: Proposes compound density networks (CDNs) that combine adaptive input-dependent mixing weights with uncountably many mixture components.
summary_en.result: CDNs yield better uncertainty estimates on out-of-distribution data and are more robust to adversarial examples than previous approaches.
summary_en.validation: Empirically validated on standard benchmark datasets using maximum likelihood and variational Bayesian inference.
